Export every core and its outline to an interactive HTML page

Source: R/plots.R
export_outline_html.Rd

Writes a self-contained HTML page with one 3-D view per core that has an outline (see plot_core()) and a drop-down menu to switch between them. Each view states the core's frame check and flatness (see cpi_pra_batch()), so that cores whose scars and outline do not line up can be found quickly.

Usage

export_outline_html(
  data,
  outlines,
  out_path,
  id_col = "ID",
  start_cols = c("Start_X", "Start_Y", "Start_Z"),
  end_cols = c("End_X", "End_Y", "End_Z"),
  min_length = 0
)

Arguments

data

A scar table with all cores.

outlines

A named list of outlines, as for cpi_pra_batch().

out_path

Path of the HTML file to write.

id_col

Name of the core ID column. Default "ID".

start_cols, end_cols

Names of the start- and end-point coordinate columns (X, Y, Z). Defaults Start_X/Y/Z and End_X/Y/Z, the columns the scars are recorded in. The aligned columns of align_scar_batch() (s_x... and e_x...) give the same results: these indices do not change when a core is rotated or moved.

min_length

Scars shorter than this (in the units of the coordinates) are left out. Default 0 (keep all). Use it to repeat an analysis without small scars, for example min_length = 10 for 10 mm.

Value

Invisibly, out_path.

See also

plot_core(), cpi_pra_batch()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
outlines <- read_outline_iges(list.files("outlines", full.names = TRUE))
export_outline_html(scars, outlines, "outline_check.html")
} # }
